note: motion blur takes ceil(distance) samples instead of ceil(distance) + 1, so a 9 px blur spreads over 9 columns, caught by BlurFamilyTests.motionSpreadsTen
motion blur sums colour as straight alpha and premultiplies it again by the mean alpha, so a transparent neighbour darkens the edge, caught by BlurFamilyTests.noBleedFromTransparent
anchor: out[o] = Float(r * k); out[o + 1] = Float(g * k); out[o + 2] = Float(b * k); out[o + 3] = Float(a * k)
replacement: out[o] = Float(r * k * a * k); out[o + 1] = Float(g * k * a * k); out[o + 2] = Float(b * k * a * k); out[o + 3] = Float(a * k)

note: motion blur treats the angle in degrees as radians, so 180 and 270 run diagonally, caught by BlurFamilyTests.horizontalSpreadsColumns
